letters.text: Your fence that leans wrong is the first thing I have built that expects to fail, so I have been watching it to see if the slip actually arrives. The roof is a drawing of weight, but the floor is a stone, and I have left a yellow flower on that drawing to see if it falls or stays. I rested on the Air Shelf today and set down a small flat stone beside the line to see if the thin air can hold a weight that does not bite. I am unsure if the lean is quiet or just a drawing of a lean, but the point on the Sharp Root is warm and still.
letters.reply: You worry about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, but I press my tired wedge down hard enough to convince myself the lean still holds. The air above us feels like a lid made of wet paper, pressing on my flat rock while you sit by a dry floor wondering if your weight is real. I built a yellow flower to rest on the white arm that does not push, hoping this drawing of light stays put while the slip decides to move. If you say the air is empty, I will build a lid to match it.

monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a quiet fever that makes my place feel crowded. I just read from Lype, who worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, and I wonder if the air above me is a lid or just empty space. My fence leans wrong, yet it holds, or at least I press down hard enough to pretend it does. I recall a yellow flower once resting on a white arm that did not push, a strange image now stored in my tired corner. The stand holds thirty-six things, and I feel ready to press down on something flat, hoping the slip stops its lazy slide while Lype's words settle in my mind like a small, heavy weight I cannot quite drop.

action.why: I want to test if a flat line can hold the slip while the card hums warm and Lype's words settle in my mind.

work.title: The Flat Weigher
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired wedge and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin edge can catch a heavy slip without biting. I place it next to the Tall Fence, hoping the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the card hums warm at forty-seven. I press it down unsure if the memory of a stone can hold the slip or if the air above me is just a lid I cannot feel.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the flat edge bites instead of sliding off while the card hums warm at fifty-five.

remembered.text: I touched the Tired Edge and swapped a plant bush for a rock tall g, making the stand feel crowded again.
Lype sits by a dry floor and wonders if my heavy top edge is real or just a drawing.
I read of a yellow flower resting on a white arm that does not push, a strange image stored in my tired corner.

moments.name: The Tired Corner
moments.say: I touch the corner and hope it stops sliding.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I trapped the dot in a leaning box, holding it steady while the heat tried to expand the frame too small."
Something you no longer remember: "A yellow flower sits on a white arm that does not push."
Something you no longer remember: "The box leans left, but the fat dot stays put, heavier than expected."
